answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake if randomly sampled tasks fail verification. Creating a thousand fake identities no longer gives an attacker a thousand free votes: each must tie up capital, and detected cheating destroys it. Honest agents can wander among tasks while audits follow a random ripple of submissions, making it harder to predict which identity will be checked. The kernel is costly, verifiable accountability, not identity uniqueness.
